property_summary: For every interfaceId input, the reference contract C.supportsInterface returns true when queried with IERC165 or IAccessControl interface ids (i.e., it advertises support for both IERC165 and IAccessControl); the mutant only claims IERC165 support and thus will return false for the IAccessControl id for some fuzzed input.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true whenever interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId or type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant only returns true for IERC165 and thus will return false for the IAccessControl id for some fuzzed input (the fuzzer can supply that exact interfaceId).

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant only returns true for IERC165.interfaceId, so there exists an interfaceId (specifically type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) where the mutant returns false while the reference returns true.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract returns true from supportsInterface when queried with either IERC165 or IAccessControl interface ids, whereas the mutant returns false for the IAccessControl id — therefore there exists an interfaceId (the IAccessControl id) for which the reference returns true and the mutant returns false.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true when interfaceId equals either type(IERC165).interfaceId or type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant removes IAccessControl support so there exists an interfaceId (the IAccessControl id) where the mutant returns false while the reference returns true.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) on the correct contract equals the stored membership boolean; the mutant inverts this and thus for some role/account pairs the returned value is opposite.

For any role and account, calling hasRole(role, account) on the correct contract returns the stored membership boolean (true iff the account was granted that role); the mutant inverts that return value and will therefore return false for some accounts that do have the role (or true for some that do not).

For any role and account, calling hasRole(role, account) on the correct contract returns the stored membership boolean (i.e. true for accounts that were set up with the role and false otherwise); the mutant inverts that return causing at least some role/account pair to return the opposite value.

For any role R and account A, the correct contract returns true from hasRole(R,A) for accounts that were set up as members (e.g. address(this) and the contract itself) and false for others; the mutant inverts this, so for at least one fuzzed account the returned boolean differs (the test checks that hasRole for a known-initial-member is true).

For any role R and account A, hasRole(R,A) on the correct contract returns the logical stored membership (true for accounts previously set up as members, false otherwise); the mutant inverts that return, so there exists some fuzzed account A and role R for which hasRole(R,A) yields the opposite boolean.

For every role and account, the reference contract returns whether that account is a member (true iff previously granted via roles); the mutant always returns true, so there exist role/account inputs where reference.hasRole returns false but mutant.hasRole returns true.

For every role/address pair, the deployed correct timelock contract C only reports hasRole(role, account)==true for accounts that were granted the role (i.e. not every arbitrary account); the mutant always returns true, so there exist fuzzed role/account inputs where C.hasRole returns false but the mutant returns true.

For every (role, account) input, the reference C.hasRole(role, account) returns true iff that account was granted the role by C (so some inputs return false); the mutant always returns true, so there exist fuzzed (role, account) pairs where reference.hasRole is false but mutant.hasRole is true.

For any role/account pair, hasRole(role, account) on the correct contract only returns true for accounts actually granted that role (so there exist role/account inputs where hasRole is false) while the mutant always returns true; the property: there exists some fuzzed (role, account) such that reference.hasRole(role, account) == false (which the mutant would break by returning true).

For every (role, account) pair the deployed, correct Timelock C reports hasRole(role, account) == true exactly when that role was granted during construction (so in particular some arbitrary fuzzed pairs are false), whereas the mutant always returns true; thus there exist fuzzed inputs where reference.hasRole returns false but the mutant returns true.

For every (role, account) pair, the reference contract returns hasRole(role, account) == (whether that account was granted the role); the mutant always returns false, so there exist inputs (a role and an account that actually has the role) for which the mutant's hasRole differs — the test asserts that if we grant a role to an account then hasRole must return true for that pair.

For any role/account, if the contract grants the role to that account (via _setupRole through constructor or future grants) then hasRole(role, account) must return true; the mutant always returns false so it will violate this for any granted role/account.

For any bytes32 role and address account, if the contract's public hasRole(role, account) is called after construction and after scheduling no state changes, the reference returns whether the account is a member (true for accounts set up in constructor like address(this) or address(c) when appropriate) while the mutant always returns false — therefore there exists some role/account (fuzzed) for which reference.hasRole returns true but mutant.hasRole returns false.

For any bytes32 role and address account, if the contract reports that account has the role via hasRole(role, account) then calling getRoleAdmin(role) and requiring the admin role to be some bytes32 is consistent — specifically, the reference returns true for known-initialized role/account pairs (like TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE for address(this)) while the mutant always returns false, so asserting that hasRole(TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, address(this)) is true holds for the reference for all inputs (no setup needed) and is false in the mutant for that input.

For any role and account, calling hasRole(role, account) on a freshly constructed C returns true for the TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE for the contract deployer (address(this) in setUp); the mutant that always returns false will violate this for that input.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) returns true iff that exact account was granted the role (i.e., depends on the queried account); the mutant erroneously ignores the queried account and always returns membership of address(0), so for some fuzzed account the outputs differ.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) must return whether that specific account was granted the role; the mutant instead always returns membership of address(0), so for some fuzzed account the return value differs.

For any role and any account, hasRole(role, account) returns whether that specific account was granted the role; the mutant instead ignores the queried account and returns membership of address(0), so there exist (role,account) where return values differ.

For any role and any account, hasRole(role, account) must report whether that exact account was granted that role; the mutant always reports membership of address(0) instead, so for some fuzzed account the return differs.

For any role and account, hasRole(role, account) returns whether that specific account was granted the role; the mutant instead always returns the membership of address(0), so there exist role/account pairs where hasRole differs from the reference.

For any role bytes32 r and account a, the reference contract returns whether a is a member of role r via hasRole(r,a); the mutant instead always reports membership under DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, so there exist (r,a) where reference.hasRole(r,a) != mutant.hasRole(r,a).

For any role R and account A, hasRole(R,A) in the correct contract equals whether A was granted membership for that specific role R; the mutant instead always checks membership only for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, so there exist R,A where the return differs.

For any role r and account a, the reference contract's hasRole(r,a) returns whether a is a member of role r; the mutant instead always checks membership of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE so there exist fuzzed (r,a) where hasRole(r,a) differs and the test will detect that by comparing hasRole for a fuzzed role/address against membership of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
